module.name: speakcard
module.description: A language-learning sentence card: main sentence + smaller translation + optional reading note, each speakable with machine TTS (Web Speech / VOICEVOX) via the app's window.mdpTts API. Interactive: the speak buttons never advance the slide.
module.aiSpec:
Use for language-teaching slides (e.g. technical English): shows a MAIN sentence with a speak button, a smaller SUB line (the translation), and an optional READING NOTE (e.g. "100 °C = one hundred degrees Celsius"). Clicking a speak button reads that line aloud with the app's TTS (window.mdpTts): the narrator is picked automatically from the line's language, or named explicitly. While speaking, the words being read are highlighted in place (word-by-word for Web Speech; an approximate progressive fill for VOICEVOX). Requires an MDP build that exposes window.mdpTts; the buttons are inert (no crash) on older builds.
Block module: 1–3 body sections split by `<!-- @ -->`: section 1 — the main sentence (Markdown; e.g. the English sentence) section 2 — the sub line / translation, rendered smaller (optional) section 3 — a reading note, rendered small in accent color, never spoken (optional) To flip the direction (Japanese main, English sub) just swap the texts AND set mainlang: ja-JP, sublang: en-US.
Parameters: • mainlang (text, default en-US) — language of the main sentence (BCP-47; drives narrator pick). • sublang (text, default ja-JP) — language of the sub line. • subspeak (boolean, default false) — also give the sub line a speak button (default: only the main sentence is speakable). • mainvoice (text, default '') — narrator for the main line by name, substring ok (e.g. Zira). • subvoice (text, default '') — narrator for the sub line (Web Speech name). • speaker (number, default -1) — VOICEVOX style id used for whichever line is Japanese (-1 = don't use VOICEVOX; falls back to Web Speech automatically if the engine is down). • rate (number, default 1) — speaking rate for both lines (0.5–2; slower for learners). • highlight (boolean, default true) — highlight the words as they are spoken. • size (select sm|md|lg, default md) — overall text scale. • color (color, default var(--accent-color)) — speak-button and reading-note color.
The card itself is UNDECORATED (no frame/background) — wrap it in @callout, @bubble, @infobox etc. when a framed look is wanted.
Example: <!-- @speakcard mainlang: en-US, sublang: ja-JP, mainvoice: Zira, rate: 0.9 --> Water **boils** at 100 °C at atmospheric pressure. <!-- @ --> 水は大気圧下で 100 °C で沸騰する． <!-- @ --> 100 °C = *one hundred degrees Celsius* <!-- @end -->

param.name: mainlang
param.label: Main language
param.desc: BCP-47 language of the main sentence (picks the narrator), e.g. en-US, ja-JP.

param.name: sublang
param.label: Sub language
param.desc: BCP-47 language of the sub (translation) line.

param.name: subspeak
param.label: Sub speakable
param.desc: Also give the sub (translation) line a speak button.

param.name: mainvoice
param.label: Main narrator
param.desc: Web Speech narrator for the main line, by name (substring ok, e.g. Zira). Blank = auto by language.

param.name: subvoice
param.label: Sub narrator
param.desc: Web Speech narrator for the sub line. Blank = auto by language.

param.name: speaker
param.label: VOICEVOX speaker
param.desc: VOICEVOX style id for the Japanese line (-1 = use Web Speech).

param.name: highlight
param.label: Read-along highlight
param.desc: Highlight the words as they are spoken.

param.name: size
param.label: Size
param.desc: Overall text scale of the card.

snippet.description: English sentence + smaller Japanese translation + reading note; both lines speakable.

snippet.label: Speak card (named narrator)
snippet.text: <!-- @speakcard mainvoice: Zira, rate: 0.85 --> Several methods **have been proposed** to reduce noise. <!-- @ --> ノイズを低減するための手法がいくつか提案されてきた． <!-- @end -->
snippet.description: Pick the narrator by name (e.g. Zira for en-US).

snippet.label: Speak card (VOICEVOX 和訳)
